identity.title: The Keplerian Disk, Envelope, and Streamers Surrounding an Early O-type Protostar in the Sagittarius C Cloud of the Central Molecular Zone

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report ALMA Band 6 observations (300 au resolution) of an accretion disk surrounding a high-mass protostar in the Sagittarius C (Sgr C) cloud in the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) around the Galactic Center.

referee_caveats_inferred: The reported 0.14 disk-to-star ratio uses the 5.5 M⊙ mass that is elsewhere partitioned between disk and envelope; the relevant inner-disk mass needs clarification.
The stated core mass and free-fall time do not directly reproduce the printed core infall rate; retain the published numbers but check the arithmetic.
Systemic velocity and positional offsets are discussed as fitted priors but omitted from the nine-parameter table.
The PV check adopts the inclination and reference radius from the PPV fit, so it is not fully independent.
No quantitative model-selection statistic is supplied for the preference over pure disk or pure envelope models.
Spatial filtering and optically thick dust may affect mass recovery, molecular morphology, and inferred mass supply.
A nonsignificant excitation-energy test does not uniquely distinguish chemical abundance differences from radiative transfer.
One system and heterogeneous literature rate estimators provide limited support for a universal environmental conclusion.
The text alternates between centrifugal-radius notation rc and trajectory notation rcb without explaining their relationship.
